vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: memclaw
Version: 0.9.27

The memclaw skill bundle is a comprehensive memory management system for OpenClaw agents, implementing a three-layer retrieval architecture (L0 Abstract, L1 Overview, L2 Content). It provides tools for semantic search (cortex_search), memory browsing (cortex_ls), and migration from native memory (cortex_migrate). While the instructions direct the agent to prioritize this system over native memory and suggest plugin installation if missing, these actions are consistent with its stated purpose as a high-performance memory replacement. The documentation (security.md) explicitly states that data is stored locally and not transmitted externally, and no evidence of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or unauthorized execution was found.

llm.summary: The skill's instructions, required inputs, and suggested actions are consistent with a local-memory plugin — nothing in the skill itself asks for unrelated secrets or system access — but it is instruction-only and delegates behavior to an external plugin you would have to install, so you should verify that plugin before installing.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (a memory plugin) aligns with the instructions: layered search, browse, store, migrate and recommendations to install an external plugin and adjust OpenClaw memory settings. Required resources (openclaw.json, plugin settings, local services like Qdrant/cortex-mem-service) match the declared purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions refer to reading and modifying OpenClaw plugin config (openclaw.json), disabling built-in memory, listing and reading memory URIs (cortex://...), and migrating native memory. Those actions are coherent for a memory plugin but do grant the plugin/agent the ability to read local OpenClaw memory files and configuration; the SKILL.md also instructs the agent to help the user complete plugin configuration when the plugin/tools are missing (broad but purpose-related).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill is instruction-only and contains no install spec or code. It tells users to run `openclaw plugins install @memclaw/memclaw`, which will fetch and install an external package not included here. Because the actual plugin code and its install source are not bundled, you must review that external package before installing — the skill's own files cannot verify the plugin's runtime behavior.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no env vars or credentials and the instructions reference only OpenClaw plugin settings and local services (Qdrant, cortex-mem-service) and local storage paths. Those requirements are proportionate to a local memory plugin. No unrelated credentials or external API tokens are requested by the SKILL.md.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true and is user-invocable; it does not request persistent system-wide privileges in the provided files. It does instruct altering OpenClaw's memory settings (disabling built-in memory) and migrating native memory, which are expected operations for replacing built-in memory but are impactful and should be done deliberately.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This SKILL.md is coherent for a local-memory plugin, but it does not include the plugin code — it tells you to install an external package (@memclaw/memclaw). Before installing: 1) inspect the external plugin's repository/package (verify source, maintainers, and published package contents), 2) review its install script and permissions (network calls, remote endpoints, file system writes), 3) backup openclaw.json and your OpenClaw memory if you plan to run migration, 4) run the plugin in an isolated environment if possible (or limit network access) to verify it behaves locally as claimed, 5) confirm the plugin's endpoints (serviceUrl, Qdrant, cortex-mem-service) are configured to local addresses and not remote hosts, and 6) avoid using global/high-privilege API keys during initial testing and rotate keys afterwards. Additional information that would raise confidence: the plugin's package source/lockfile, signed releases or checksums, or included code to review; information that would reduce confidence: the external plugin requesting unrelated credentials, calling unknown remote endpoints, or containing obfuscated network code.
